cells.tense: You are standing here with the pen in your hand and the next move already underway.
cells.ask: Write the decision you keep circling, plus the first thing you will do about it, on paper today.
cells.core:
You don't have to raise your voice here. You hold what's in front of you and it stays where you put it. There's also a direction moving through what you do — it doesn't need announcing first, and it doesn't need anyone to agree. When you decide, the deciding is quick, and it lands.

What carries the weight isn't brittle. Pressure presses on it and the shape stays. The growing edge is letting that shape meet a few more people before it's fully set, not to prove anything, but because what serves what it holds has to know what's pressing on it. Say the direction out loud, once, in a sentence, this week.

cells.tense: You are bracing against a version of this that hasn't happened yet, and the bracing is doing the holding.
cells.ask: Put one thing you've been planning for on today's page, then leave it alone until tomorrow.
cells.core:
You're carrying more than today handed you. Somewhere ahead the thing has to take its final form — the right call, the moment it all has to go through — and you're bearing that version now, before it exists. The weight in your shoulders is real. Most of what's on them hasn't happened.

The form that would serve you here is plainer than the one you're building. Clear structure can wait to be seen; it doesn't need every wall drawn before the ground is broken. What arrives this week is small and actual. Let the future version stay unbuilt a while longer, and put your weight on the part that is here.

cells.tense: You are still at a door that is already behind you, and your body hasn't moved on from what it took to stand there.
cells.ask: Make one small thing this week — a list, a repair, a plan — and let it be done, not perfect.
cells.core:
The keeping-going happens. What's thinner is the contact with it — you can carry a thing and still be somewhere else while it gets carried. There's strength in you; what's quieter is the sense of moving through your own day rather than standing at the edge of it, deciding whether to come in.

Don't try to feel your way back. Build instead. Make one small thing that stands up by itself when you set it down — not a feeling, an object, a task finished. The making puts charge back into what's gone still, and standing on your own day gets easier. Come through at whatever pace you can stand.

cells.tense: You are already steering through this and you describe it as the thing happening by itself.
cells.ask: Name one thing you arranged or kept steady this week and say out loud that you did it.
cells.core:
You've been keeping this up for a while — the form in place, the pressure off, the direction moving. When you talk about it you talk as if the shape arranged itself. It didn't. You did. The clarity other people notice isn't luck. It's you, doing it, and not marking it as yours.

The more settled the form gets, the less likely you are to claim you built it. There's no drama in that, which is exactly why it passes unclaimed — by you most of all. You don't need to announce it to anyone. Just take the pen back into your hand long enough to say, once, that this is yours.
